source_text: XXII. Τοιοῦτον βίον διανύσας ὁ μακάριος Πιόνιος ἀμώμητον ἀνέγκλητον ἀδιάφθορον, ἀεὶ τὴν γνώμην ἔχων τεταμένην εἰς θεὸν παντοκράτορα καὶ εἰς τὸν μεσίτην θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν, τοιούτου κατηξιώθη τέλους, καὶ τὸν μέγαν ἀγῶνα νικήσας διῆλθε διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας εἰς τὸ πλατὺ καὶ μέγα φῶς. ἐσημάνθη δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ στέφανος καὶ διὰ τοῦ σώματος. μετὰ γὰρ τὸ κατασβεσθῆναι τὸ πῦρ τοιοῦτον αὐτὸν εἴδομεν οἱ παραγενόμενοι ὁποῖόν τε τὸ σῶμα ἀκμάζοντος ἀθλητοῦ κεκοσμημένου. καὶ γὰρ τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ [μίλλα — cod.; sense: reddened] γένοντο καὶ αἱ τρίχες ἐν χρῷ τῆς κεφαλῆς προσεκάθηντο, τὸ δὲ γένειον αὐτοῦ ὡς ἰούλοις ἐπανθοῦσιν ἐκεκόσμητο. ἐπέλαμπε δὲ καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, πάλιν χάρις θαυμαστή, ὥστε τοὺς Χριστιανοὺς στηριχθῆναι μᾶλλον τῇ πίστει, τοὺς δὲ [ἀπίστους — scan Ainiorovs] πτοηθέντας καὶ τὸ συνειδὸς ἔχοντας πεφοβημένον κατελθεῖν. XXIII. Ταῦτα ἐπράχθη ἐπὶ ἀνθυπάτου τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουλίου Πρόκλου Κυντιλλιανοῦ, ὑπατευόντων αὐτοκράτορος Μεσίου Κίντου Τραιανοῦ Δεκίου Σεβαστοῦ τὸ δεύτερον καὶ Οὐεττίου Γράτου, πρὸ τεσσάρων εἰδῶν Μαρτίων κατὰ Ῥωμαίους, κατὰ δὲ Ἀσιανοὺς μηνὸς ἕκτου ἐννεακαιδεκάτῃ, ἡμέρᾳ σαββάτῳ, ὥρᾳ δεκάτῃ, κατὰ δὲ ἡμᾶς βασιλεύοντος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.
pass_a_gloss: Literal gloss: having completed such a life, the blessed Pionius, blameless unaccused incorrupt, ever holding his mind stretched toward God almighty and toward the mediator of God and men Jesus Christ our Lord, was deemed worthy of such an end, and having conquered the great contest he passed through the narrow door into the broad and great light; and his crown was signified also through the body; for after the fire was quenched we who were present saw him such as is the body of a flourishing adorned athlete; for both his ears became reddened and the hairs clung to the skin of the head, and his beard was adorned as with blooming down; and his face shone, again a wonderful grace, so that the Christians were strengthened rather in faith, and the unbelievers, having been frightened and having a terrified conscience, went down; these things were done under the proconsul of Asia Julius Proclus Quintillianus, in the consulship of emperor Messius Quintus Trajanus Decius Augustus for the second time and Vettius Gratus, four days before the Ides of March by Roman reckoning, by Asian reckoning on the nineteenth of the sixth month, on Saturday, at the tenth hour, but by our reckoning while our Lord Jesus Christ reigns, to whom be glory unto ages of ages, amen.
pass_b_english: Having completed such a life, the blessed Pionius, blameless and unimpeached and undefiled, with his mind ever bent upon God almighty and upon the mediator of God and men, Jesus Christ our Lord (1 Timothy 2:5), was counted worthy of such an end, and after winning the great contest he passed through the narrow door (Matthew 7:13) into the wide and great light.
His crown was made visible through his body as well, for after the fire was quenched we who were present saw him like the body of an athlete in his prime and in full adornment.
His ears had become reddened, and the hairs lay close upon the skin of his head, and his beard was adorned as with fresh down coming into bloom.
His face also shone, a marvelous grace again, so that the Christians were established still more firmly in faith, while the unbelievers drew back in terror with stricken conscience.

These things were done when Julius Proclus Quintilianus was proconsul of Asia, in the consulship of the emperor Messius Quintus Trajanus Decius Augustus for the second time and Vettius Gratus, four days before the Ides of March by Roman reckoning, by Asian reckoning on the nineteenth of the sixth month, on the Sabbath day, at the tenth hour, but by our reckoning while our Lord Jesus Christ reigns, to whom be glory unto the ages of ages, amen.

lemmas.gloss: having completed a course of life here

choices.why: Accusative in apposition to Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, preserving the exact Pauline phrasing rather than generalizing to intercessor.

choices.term: διῆλθε διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας εἰς τὸ πλατὺ καὶ μέγα φῶς
choices.english: passed through the narrow door into the broad and great light
choices.why: διὰ with genitive is spatial passage, and πλατὺ contrasts στενῆς; keeps door/light antithesis instead of moralizing to gate of heaven.

choices.term: ἐσημάνθη δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ στέφανος καὶ διὰ τοῦ σώματος
choices.english: his crown was also marked out through his body
choices.why: Passive ἐσημάνθη with διὰ plus genitive gives means of manifestation, not location; keeps visible sign sense.
